newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares end with small gains, BHEL up 7 pct.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares end with small gains, BHEL up 7 pct.

text.p: Shares at Bombay exchanges ended with small gains on Thursday, after end-account factors and lack of any new political developments checked a mid-session rally, dealers said.
"The markets are moving sideways," said R. Ramakrishnan, chief dealer at ASK-Raymond James India Ltd. "There is not much downward pressure, but the market is stuck in a narrow band."

Shares of state-run Bharat Heavy Electrical Ltd (BHEL) surged 22.50 rupees, or seven percent, to 352.50 rupees after the firm on Thursday announced a 34 percent jump in its 1996/97 (April-March) net profit to 4.68 billion rupees.
The better-than expected annual results spurred hectic buying interest amid sharp volumes, traders said.

"The stock rocketed after the announcement of results. Speculators were aggressive bidders," said a dealer at a local brokerage. By close, more than 793,000 shares were traded at the Bombay Stock Exchange.

Lack of any new political developments led to dull trade among bellwether stocks on Thursday. But brokers said they were pinning hopes on the safe passage of the 1997/98 (April-March) pro-business budget despite a current political crisis.
A broad consensus emerging among political parties to pass the budget through parliament helped firm the market mood, players said.
Parliament had earlier been scheduled to take up the budget after reconvening on April 21.

Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's 15-party minority coalition government has to face a trust vote in parliament on April 11 after the Congress party on Sunday withdrew make-or-break support, plunging the country into political uncertainty.
